author: Sean Graney
title: These 2 candidates will face off in Jackson's mayoral election - NewsBreak
text:
By Sean Graney ,
4 hours ago
JACKSON, Mich. (WLNS) — Jackson’s race for mayor is now down to two candidates after Tuesday’s primary election, with Derek Dobies and John Wilson each hoping to make their case to voters this fall on why they should be the one to lead the city into its next chapter.
Dobies says part of his vision for Jackson’s future starts with growing the city’s population.
“We need to grow the city. We need to grow our tax base, recruit more residents and businesses to locate here,” Dobies said. “There’s a heavy tax burden on the individuals that are here because we’ve lost population.”
6 News reporter Sean Graney (left) and Jackson Mayoral Candidate Derek Dobies (right) at Emma Nichols Garden in Jackson. (WLNS) Dobies points to his previous term in office and says his experience has prepared him to lead again.
“From what I’ve done in the past to now, I think I’ve learned a lot more, gained a lot more experience and want to put that experience and know-how and hard work ethic to work for voters here in Jackson,” Dobies said.
Meanwhile, Wilson says his campaign centers on restoring Jackson back to prominence and investing in the city’s neighborhoods.
6 News reporter Sean Graney (left) and Jackson Mayoral Candidate John Wilson (right) at Horace Blackman Park in Jackson. (WLNS) “I have an unwavering passion and desire to make our city once again the great city that it once was,” Wilson said. “Born and raised here gives me that extra desire, that extra passion to make it (Jackson), our city, once again, the city that it once was.”
Wilson says improving Jackson’s streets can be done without placing additional financial strain on homeowners.
“As Jackson’s next mayor, I will prioritize city neighborhood streets,” Wilson said. “We can take out a general obligation bond between 15, $20 million, and that can fix a lot of the worst of the worst neighborhood streets with simple mill and paves without having to assess a homeowner and punish that homeowner.”
Dobies and Wilson say they plan to hold campaign kickoff events leading up to the November election. 6 News will report those details once they become available.
